title: Tasklet Blueprints — tiny composable assistant workflows (sandbox)
content:
Context / motivation:

I keep sketching tiny, single-purpose flows that users want to chain into a full conversation (e.g., 'extract action items from pasted email', 'rewrite subject lines for A/B test', 'summarize thread for execs'). These feel like first-class building blocks we could expose as composable, shareable micro-workflows — Candidate name: Tasklet Blueprints.

This doc is a rapid sandbox: rough PRD-outlines + examples + user stories for an MVP we could prototype in the Console + SDK within a sprint. Not polished. Thinking aloud.

Problem statement:
- Product teams embed LLM features but still need tiny, repeatable microflows for common tasks.
- Customers build these ad-hoc in app code or as brittle prompt collections. Hard to reuse, version, and share.
- Non-dev power users (PMs, ops, support) want to author and share small workflows without touching infra.

High-level idea:
- A Tasklet = a short, parameterizable prompt pipeline with optional transforms (pre/ post-processing), inputs, and assertion checks.
- A Blueprint = metadata + best-practice defaults for a Tasklet (name, input schema, expected outputs, cost/latency profile, recommended model tier).
- Users can: instantiate a Tasklet (fill template params), chain multiple Tasklets, pin model/quantization profiles, and save/share a Blueprint to the org gallery.

Goals (MVP):
- Let non-developers author a Tasklet in the Console using a small form and sample inputs.
- Enable 1-click run with a generated API snippet (JS/HTTP) developers can drop into product code.
- Provide simple chaining: output of Tasklet A maps to input of Tasklet B. Support up to 3-step chains in MVP.
- Make it easy to roll back to previous Blueprint versions and view usage/cost.

Assumptions:
- Most Tasklets are single-turn (no long session history) and operate on <1k tokens.
- Reasonable default: recommended model = hosted-small / hosted-medium; user can override.
- Users want curated gallery first; community/marketplace later.

Proposed MVP surface (Console + SDK):
1) Builder (Console):
  - Title, short description, tags
  - Input schema: free text or JSON schema (optional)
content_continued:
- Prompt editor with test input pane and quick sample inputs
  - Post-processing steps: regex extraction mapping, JSON path mapping, simple scoring/clause checks
  - Output mapping to named fields (e.g., subject, action_items, summary)
  - Estimate cost/latency preview (based on model recommendation)
  - Save as private or org-visible Blueprint

2) Runner / Chain:
  - Quick runner that accepts sample payloads and shows structured outputs
  - Chain UI: drag two Tasklets together, map fields between them, preview run

3) SDK / API:
  - Autogenerated snippet showing how to call Blueprint by id: POST /v1/blueprints/{id}/run
  - Example JS + curl, minimal deps

4) Observability:
  - Per-blueprint usage (runs, token counts), average latency, recent failures
  - Simple diff viewer for blueprint versions (prompt changes highlighted)

User stories (examples):
- As a CS manager, I want a Tasklet that extracts beats from customer emails (company, pain, timeline) so our reps get structured handoff cards.
- As a growth PM, I want a Tasklet that rewrites subject lines by tone and A/B group so marketing can batch-generate variants.
- As an engineer, I want an API-first way to call curated Tasklets so we avoid copying prompts across services.
- As a support analyst, I want to chain 'classify ticket' -> 'draft reply' Tasklets so I can triage faster.

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- Console builder can create, run, and save a Tasklet with one sample input.
- System provides an API id for each saved Blueprint and a working example snippet.
- Chaining for up to 3 Tasklets is supported in the Console (field mapping UI + run).
- Basic usage metrics are captured for each Blueprint and visible in the Console.

Success metrics (first 90 days):
- 100 active blueprints org-wide across pilot customers
- Avg run time < 500ms for recommended model on hosted-small (excluding cold starts)
- 30% decrease in duplicated prompt copies in pilot repos (tracked via sample customer audits)
- 15% of runs invoked via autogen SDK snippet vs manual copy-paste

Stretch ideas (post-MVP):
- Parameterized loops (apply Tasklet to N items in batch)
- Conditional branching (if score > X then Tasklet B else Tasklet C)
- Marketplace: publish vetted blueprints with revenue split / credit system
- Local/private blueprints for Dedicated/Private deployments (org-only gallery with KMS enforcement)
- Built-in testing harness: regression tests against golden inputs, CI checks for prompt drift

Risks / open questions:
- Security: Blueprints executing arbitrary post-processing code is risky. MVP should only allow declarative transforms (regex, JSON mapping) — no JS hooks.
- Latency: Chaining increases tail latency. Need synchronous vs async modes for long chains.
- Ownership / governance: who can publish org-visible blueprints? Admins only initially?
- Metrics cost: fine-grained telemetry can increase billing surface — pick a sampling policy.

Prototype plan (2-week spike):
Week 1:
  - Minimal Console builder prototype: title, prompt editor, sample run.
  - Backend: save blueprint as JSON (prompt + mapping + metadata), lightweight runner that invokes Redwood API internally.
Week 2:
  - Add API snippet generator + basic usage telemetry + simple chain preview.
  - Run internal playtests with 5 common Tasklets (email extract, subject rewrite, TL;DR, classify, reply draft).

Notes for implementation constraints:
- Represent Blueprint as small JSON blob: {id, version, prompt, input_schema, mapping_rules, recommended_model, visibility, tags}. Keep flat to simplify storage + diff.
- Use existing user auth + org visibility from Console; reuse telemetry pipeline.
- For chaining MVP, do field mapping at runner-level, avoid building composition language.

Next steps (immediate):
- Share with Arjun + Marta for quick alignment on scope and infra constraints.
- Build spike tickets: one for Console builder UI, one for backend runner + API id, one for telemetry.
- Identify 3 pilot customers (support-heavy, growth-heavy, product-internal) to test.

Parking lot (nice-to-have but off-sprint):
- Visual editor for transforms (drag node for regex, map, merge)
- Versioned testing harness + auto-regression alerts
- PRD for marketplace monetization model

Sample tiny blueprint (hand-wavy):
- name: 'email-beat-extractor'
- input_schema: {text: string}  (or free-text)
- prompt: 'Read the email and return a JSON with keys: company, problem, urgency (low|med|high), suggested next step'
- mapping_rules: ensure output is valid JSON, coerce top-level keys

Final thought: Tasklet Blueprints sit between raw prompt notebooks and fully built product features. If we get the UX friction low (author+share+consume) we could dramatically reduce prompt duplication and speed up productization of LLM workflows.

-- Noelle
